core_obligations: Choose representatives (proof lines 4005-4006): the author computes the derived pullback on a K-flat complex with flat terms and the derived pushforward on a K-injective complex.

Transport the abelian adjunction (proof lines 4006-4008): with those representatives the abelian adjunction between pullback and pushforward identifies the two hom groups appearing in the statement, which gives the bifunctorial adjunction on the derived categories.
proof_roadmap: Use a K-flat representative for the source and a K-injective representative for the target.
Apply the abelian adjunction between pullback and pushforward to identify the hom groups.
Conclude the bifunctorial adjunction of derived functors.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the derived pullback constructed earlier in the chapter is left adjoint to the derived pushforward, with the displayed bifunctorial identification of hom groups (statement lines 3989-4003). The proof chooses representatives on which the derived functors are computed naively (proof lines 4005-4006) and transports the abelian adjunction between pullback and pushforward to those representatives (proof lines 4006-4008). The non-formal content is the choice of representatives making the abelian adjunction applicable. The claim is H2: one representative choice plus one adjunction transport.
